arguments.content:
# Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm the customer's deployment is Hosted API and identify whether debug payload logging is enabled.
2. Check the executed order form, DPA, and approved retention/residency addenda for customer-specific terms.
3. Escalate backup purge, termination, residency, cross-region, legal-hold, and evidence-package questions to Security/SRE and Legal.
4. For deletion, verify the request and track completion through the support case; do not invent a backup-completion date or certificate commitment.
5. If approved facts change, revise this canonical path and replace its semantic memory rather than publishing parallel guidance.

## Evidence

Authoritative baseline:

- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-data-and-logs-retention-policy.json) — document `dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e` (published Security policy).

Conflict/validation inputs (not authority for the unknown promises above):

- [Data disposition & residency — Hosted API questionnaire](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20280220-data-disposition-hosted-api-answers-glomerate.json) — document `dsid_49ad83c4629c4d52a3873ef5c501fa5d`.
- [Residency & evidence-gathering discovery — Silverline Capital](/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/sales-calls/2026-06-05-residency-evidence-discovery-with-silverline-capital.json) — document `dsid_06b6ace6ae094712806536c0ccea07e0`.

# Hosted API retention correction — evidence matrix

Status: Draft, unindexed
Purpose: Record interpretations evaluated and rejected; not support guidance.

| Topic | Evidence | Interpretation | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default payload retention | Published Security retention policy says content is not persisted by default and debug payloads are opt-in for 7 days; Crestline questionnaire says request/response payloads default to 30 days. | Replace baseline with a universal 30-day payload-retention claim. | Rejected. The published product policy is the stronger default authority; preserve its default and treat customer-specific questionnaire wording as conflicting. |
| Primary deletion | Published policy says verified stored-data deletion within 30 days; Crestline Hosted response says primary purge within 30 days after erasure or termination. | Promise 72 hours based on other sales/questionnaire threads. | Rejected. Thirty days is corroborated and supportable; 72 hours is inconsistent and not the general outer SLA. |
| Backup purge | Crestline Hosted response says backups and replicated snapshots scrubbed within 90 days. Other threads cite 14 days, 30 days, or 30–90 days. | Promise backup purge within 14 days. | Rejected. Use the stronger approved 90-day outer window and do not turn faster operational targets into a general SLA. |
| Certified decommission | Dedicated/Private playbook provides a 10-business-day standard SLA and signed certification. | Apply that SLA and certificate format to Hosted. | Rejected. The playbook expressly scopes itself to Dedicated and Private tenants. |
| Residency | Published Hosted residency policy guarantees allowed-region processing, no out-of-set content fallback, and content-aware log boundaries. | Say all Hosted accounts are automatically single-region. | Rejected. The guarantee applies only when allowed regions are configured; no-pinning mode has no residency guarantee. |
| Backup location | Crestline response says DR replicas depend on SLA and EU-only contracts disable cross-region replication; Hosted residency policy does not universally cover backup placement. | Say every Hosted backup remains in the serving region. | Rejected. Backup locality is contract/configuration dependent. |
| Replica erasure | SRE-backed GreenBank thread documents tombstones, DeletionEvent, restore guard, replica acknowledgements, and 2–18-hour typical expunge waves. | Promise all cross-region backup erasure within 18 hours. | Rejected. The timing is operational/typical and customer-contextual, not a general SLA; use the 90-day outer customer-facing window. |
| Evidence | Crestline offers deletion attestation; GreenBank documents event IDs and per-replica acknowledgements. | Promise raw internal logs or notarization to every Hosted customer. | Rejected. Evidence format and delivery remain contract/channel dependent. |
| Legal holds | Published retention policy is silent; other sources and the Dedicated/Private playbook identify hold exceptions. | Promise unconditional deletion regardless of holds. | Rejected. Preserve the legal-hold qualification and escalate. |

# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

## Backup and cross-region qualification

Do not claim that every Hosted backup is single-region. Approved Hosted questionnaire language says backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA, while EU-only contractual configurations disable cross-region replication. The Hosted residency policy does not itself create a universal backup-location promise.

When cross-region replicas exist, the documented erasure workflow tombstones the primary object and backup manifests, emits a DeletionEvent with per-region targets, blocks restore of a tombstoned object during expunge, and reaches terminal completion only after every replica acknowledges expunge. Support may use the final event and per-replica acknowledgements as case evidence, but must not promise a particular internal expunge-wave duration as a general SLA.

## Evidence and customer responses

- For routine deletion, track the verified request, primary completion, replica/backup completion, and final attestation in the support case.
- Do not apply the 10-business-day certified-decommission SLA from the Dedicated/Private playbook to Hosted API; that playbook expressly excludes Hosted.
- Do not promise raw internal logs, storage locations, or a notarized certificate. Evidence delivery must follow the approved support/security channel and customer contract.
- Check the executed order form, DPA, residency addendum, legal holds, and approved exceptions before answering.
- Any change to Redwood-managed retention requires Security and SRE review and an update to customer-facing guidance.

## Sources

- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-data-and-logs-retention-policy.json) — `dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e`.
- [Hosted Data Residency Policy and Engineering Controls](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/hosted-data-residency-policy-and-controls.json) — `dsid_eb9f7314dd10443fbf70a80306d5119a`.
- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) — `dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`.
- [Geo backup deletion acknowledgement and cross-region restore handshake](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260607-geo-backup-delete-acknowledgement-handshake.json) — `dsid_58d93b12079648b29e41e8afb78aa7cf`.
- [Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/tenant-decommission-and-data-erase-certification-playbook-2026.json) — `dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724` (scope limitation evidence).

arguments.summary: Corrected support rule: retain the published defaults (customer content not persisted by default; opt-in debug payloads 7 days; metadata-only operational logs and no-payload traces 14 days). For verified Hosted erasure or tenant termination, use 30 days for primary purge and 90 days for backups/replicated snapshots, with an attestation on completion, subject to holds and contract terms. Configured allowed-region sets constrain customer-content processing and content-bearing logging and prevent out-of-set fallback; unpinned accounts have no residency guarantee. Backup locality is contract/SLA dependent. Cross-region erasure uses tombstones, DeletionEvent state, restore guards, and replica acknowledgements; do not promote typical internal expunge timings to a general SLA.
